programming-in-java--access-level-modifi.title: member access levels
programming-in-java--access-level-modifi.note: protected also reaches subclasses in other packages; no modifier means package-private only.

programming-in-java--method-signature.title: what counts in a method signature
rows: static and final do not distinguish
programming-in-java--method-signature.note: Two methods differing only in return type do not compile: the signature is name plus parameter types.

programming-in-java--string.title: String methods return new objects
programming-in-java--string.note: toUpperCase returns a new String; s still refers to the original, so only the reassigned u is upper case.

programming-in-java--virtual-method-invo.title: dispatch on the object, not the reference
lines: class Dog extends Animal { void speak() { System.out.println("woof"); } }
programming-in-java--virtual-method-invo.note: The reference is Animal but the object is Dog, so the JVM dispatches to Dog.speak() at run time.

programming-in-java--interface.title: interface and implementing class
programming-in-java--interface.note: Interface fields are implicitly public static final and methods public abstract; the implementation must be public.

programming-in-java--interface-versus-ab.title: interface versus abstract class
programming-in-java--interface-versus-ab.note: A class may implement several interfaces but extend only one class: interfaces buy types, abstract classes buy shared state.

programming-in-java--collection-implemen.title: common collection implementations
programming-in-java--collection-implemen.note: Hash structures trade ordering for average O(1) lookup; tree structures keep keys sorted at O(log n).

programming-in-java--catching-an-excepti.title: catching a runtime exception
programming-in-java--catching-an-excepti.note: The catch parameter names the type to handle; without it the exception would unwind the call stack.

programming-in-java--finally-block.title: finally runs before the return completes
programming-in-java--finally-block.note: finally runs after the return expression is evaluated but before control leaves f(), so cleanup is never skipped.

programming-in-java--thread.title: process versus thread
rows: a crash can end the process
programming-in-java--thread.note: Threads share the heap and open files, so they communicate cheaply but need synchronization.

programming-in-java--synchronization.title: synchronized methods lock the instance
programming-in-java--synchronization.note: Each synchronized method locks the Counter instance, so two threads cannot run inc() at the same time.

programming-in-java--layout-manager.title: Swing layout managers
rows: equal cells in r x c
programming-in-java--layout-manager.note: BorderLayout and GridLayout stretch components to fill their slot; FlowLayout and BoxLayout keep the preferred size.

programming-in-java--event-listener.title: registering an action listener
programming-in-java--event-listener.note: addActionListener registers the lambda; Swing invokes it on the event dispatch thread when the button is pressed.

programming-in-java--socket.title: TCP client socket
programming-in-java--socket.note: The constructor resolves the host and connects to the port; try-with-resources closes the socket at the end of the block.
